spec.title: fragment() on a nested field returns the results of a different field
spec.summary: A precise bug report. `Query.fragment()` (tinydb/queries.py:489-501) builds its query hash as `('fragment', freeze(document))` and leaves out `self._path`. The other path-based tests I read (`==`, `any`, `all`, `one_of`) include the path in the hash. As a result `User.home.fragment(d)` and `User.work.fragment(d)` have equal hashes and compare equal. I did not check this against the table's query cache, so the cache link is the reporter's hypothesis. The specification has one agreed core requirement (a search must return the documents matching the queried field, including when an earlier search used a different field with the same fragment document) and one candidate (queries on different paths must not compare equal). It does not design the fix. The verdict is READY-WITH-OPEN-ITEMS, not READY, because the stakeholder mode is `unavailable`. Only P3 questions are open. The issue text contained no instructions aimed at the workflow.

requirements.statement: When a search uses `Query().<field>.fragment(document)`, the system shall return exactly the stored documents whose value at `<field>` contains the key/value pairs of `document`, regardless of whether an earlier search on the same database used a different field with an equal fragment document.
requirements.source_quote: The second search gives me the result of the first one!

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB on MemoryStorage holding {'name': 'ana', 'home': {'city': 'Pune'}, 'work': {'city': 'Delhi'}} and {'name': 'raj', 'home': {'city': 'Delhi'}, 'work': {'city': 'Pune'}}, and a first search `db.search(User.home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` has already run
acceptance_criteria.when: `db.search(User.work.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` is called on the same db object
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is a list containing only the 'raj' document

acceptance_criteria.given: the same database and data, with no earlier search
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is a list containing only the 'ana' document

acceptance_criteria.given: the same database and data, with `User.work.fragment({'city': 'Pune'})` searched first
acceptance_criteria.when: `db.search(User.home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` is called on the same db object
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is a list containing only the 'ana' document

acceptance_criteria.given: the same database and data, after `db.search(User.home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'}))` has returned the 'ana' document
acceptance_criteria.when: the identical search is repeated on the same db object
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is again a list containing only the 'ana' document

requirements.statement: The system shall treat `Query().home.fragment({'city': 'Pune'})` and `Query().work.fragment({'city': 'Pune'})` as unequal queries (`==` returns False).
requirements.source_quote: Also `User.home.fragment({...}) == User.work.fragment({...})` is `True`, which surprised me.

interpretations: The table's query result cache returns an entry stored for another query, because the two queries compare equal
Some other stale-state mechanism, since a fresh TinyDB gives the correct result

open_questions.question: Should two fragment queries on different field paths with the same fragment document compare unequal, as FR-QRY-002 states, or is the equality only a symptom of the wrong search result?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The reporter says only that the equality 'surprised' them. Making it a requirement adds negation, so it stays a candidate until the maintainer accepts it.
options: (b) Drop FR-QRY-002 and keep only the search-result requirement

open_questions.question: Should other `Query` methods that use a path be checked for the same problem of leaving the path out of the query hash, or is only `fragment` in scope?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Sets the scope of the fix and tests. Only `fragment` is reported. I read `==`, `any`, `all` and `one_of` and they include the path. I did not read the others.
options: (b) Also audit the remaining path-based methods (e.g. matches, search, test, exists, comparison operators)

assumptions.text: Queries on different field paths with the same fragment document should be unequal (FR-QRY-002).
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A test for FR-QRY-002 would enforce behaviour the maintainer does not want. The impact is low, because equality of queries on different paths is hard to justify.

assumptions.text: The reporter's environment (tinydb 4.9.0, Python 3.12, Windows 11) is context only. The behaviour is platform-independent and can be reproduced with MemoryStorage.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: A platform-specific cause would not be reproduced by the pytest tests.

assumptions.text: The requester/maintainer is the decision owner for scope. No maintainer comments were supplied, so the stakeholder mode is `unavailable`.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: The scope decisions in Q-001 and Q-002 may be made by someone else.

out_of_scope: Designing or choosing the fix (for example how the hash or cache key is built)
Redesigning or removing the query cache
Changing the behaviour of query methods other than fragment unless Q-002 is answered otherwise
Changes to documentation or the public API

design.summary: Add the query path to the hash that Query.fragment builds, so fragment queries on different fields get different hashes. They then no longer compare equal, and Table.search no longer returns another field's cached result.
design.approach: In tinydb/queries.py, Query.fragment (line ~499) builds the hash as ('fragment', freeze(document)) and leaves out self._path. Table.search uses the query as the LRUCache key, and QueryInstance.__eq__ and __hash__ both rely on _hash. So User.home.fragment(d) and User.work.fragment(d) collide: the second search gets the first one's cached result, and == returns True. The fix is one line: change the hash to ('fragment', self._path, freeze(document)), the same shape that one_of uses (('one_of', self._path, freeze(items))). self._path is a tuple of str or callables, and the other path-based methods already put it in their hashes. _generate_test already sets the hash to None when the path is not cacheable. No change to Table, the cache or the public API is needed. Q-002 defaults to fragment only, so I leave other methods alone.

alternatives.option: Key the Table query cache on something other than the query hash (for example the query object identity or its path)
alternatives.why_not: The bug is in the query hash, which ADR-3 says must be unique per meaning. Changing the cache would leave == broken (FR-QRY-002) and the spec puts redesigning the cache out of scope.

alternatives.option: Audit and fix every path-based Query method (matches, search, test, exists, comparison operators) in the same change
alternatives.why_not: Q-002 defaults to fragment only, and the spec says other methods stay unchanged. It would enlarge the diff without a stated need.

alternatives.option: Disable caching for fragment queries by setting the hash to None
alternatives.why_not: This would fix the search result, but FR-QRY-002.AC-2 expects equal fragment queries on the same path to compare equal. It would also throw away caching that is legitimately possible.

files.purpose: Include the query path in the fragment hash.

symbols.name: Query.fragment
symbols.description: Change the hash tuple passed to _generate_test from ('fragment', freeze(document)) to ('fragment', self._path, freeze(document)). The test function and allow_empty_path stay the same.

ac_mapping.test_idea: Insert ana and raj into a TinyDB on MemoryStorage. Search User.home.fragment({'city':'Pune'}), then User.work.fragment({'city':'Pune'}) on the same db. Assert the second result is exactly [raj].
On a fresh db with the same data, search User.home.fragment({'city':'Pune'}) and assert the result is only ana.
Search work.fragment first, then home.fragment on the same db, and assert the second result is only ana.
Run the home.fragment search twice on the same db with a fresh Query each time, so the second run hits the cache. Assert both results are only ana.
Assert (User.home.fragment({'city':'Pune'}) == User.work.fragment({'city':'Pune'})) is False. Also assert their hashes differ.
Assert that two separately built User.home.fragment({'city':'Pune'}) queries are equal and have equal hash(), so the cache can still hit.

constraints.how_respected: The fragment hash now holds the operation tag, the path and the frozen document, as C2 requires. It is still built through Query._generate_test, which returns None for the hash when the path is not cacheable.
Table is not changed. Writes still go through _update_table and clear the cache.
queries.py keeps importing only utils. No new imports.
No new dependencies. The change reuses the existing freeze helper and self._path.

risks: Spec risk: the reporter's cache diagnosis (TERM-001) was not checked against the cache. From the code it is plausible: Table.search keys the LRUCache on the query, and equal hashes give equal keys. The tester should still check AC-1 with a real search on the same db object.
FR-QRY-002 has priority UNSET and is only an assumption (Q-001, ASM-001). Including the path in the hash makes it true as a side effect. If the maintainer rejects it, nothing needs reverting.
Other path-based methods may have the same bug (Q-002). I did not audit them, as the spec defaults to fragment only. `Query.matches`, `search`, `test` and `exists` are worth a follow-up check.
self._path can hold callables from map(). Those are hashable, and map() already sets the query hash to None through is_cacheable, so this adds no new unhashable risk.
